title: Mistral unveils Large 4 "Le Chonk" — 1.05T-parameter MoE in public preview
subtitle: The French lab's new flagship debuted at AI Everything Abu Dhabi with 49B active parameters, native multimodality, and an open-weights release planned for the end of October.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Mistral AI CEO Arthur Mensch introduced Mistral Large 4 on October 6 at AI Everything Abu Dhabi, pulling the wrap off a 1.05-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49 billion active parameters and a 1.6-billion-parameter vision encoder. The model, nicknamed "Le Chonk" by the company's engineers, is available immediately in public preview through Mistral's API, with the full open-weights release scheduled for the end of October 2026. Mistral says the system was trained from scratch over roughly two months on 4,000 Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs in the company's European data centers.

Large 4 is a hybrid design — a single checkpoint that handles instruction following, chain-of-thought reasoning, and agentic tool use rather than three separate models stitched together behind an API. The architecture activates 49B of its 1.05T parameters per token, which is the standard MoE trick for keeping serving costs down while raising headline parameter counts. The multimodal input path accepts images and documents natively through the dedicated vision encoder. Mistral has not yet published full benchmark tables, but previews quote the company positioning Large 4 against GPT-6, Gemini 4, and Claude Opus 5.5 at a fraction of their per-token prices.

The strategic read matters as much as the technical one. European policymakers have spent the year hunting for a credible open-weights alternative to the Chinese Qwen and DeepSeek families and the American frontier labs — a model that Europe-based regulators, defense buyers, and sovereign-cloud operators can run on-premise under their own compliance regime. Large 4 is Mistral's bid for that role. By committing to an open-weights drop at month-end and pricing the preview aggressively, Mistral is explicitly undercutting the proprietary pricing floor set by OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. Whether enterprises actually switch depends on how the open weights handle fine-tuning and whether the preview reasoning numbers survive independent evaluation.

A takeaway for learners: when a lab ships a trillion-parameter model as open weights, the news is not the parameter count — those stop being surprising around the time of DeepSeek V3. The news is the full stack that ships alongside it. Watch for the system card, the license text, the recommended inference stack, and the per-token price in the hosted API. Those four documents tell you whether a release is a working tool for a student or a startup, or whether it is a marketing event with weights attached. Mistral's end-of-month drop will be the real test.
